narrative_critique.headline: Timber Threshold to the River
narrative_critique.concept_statement: A timber-framed library that dissolves its ground plane into a permeable public threshold, drawing the city across an open datum toward framed river views. The parti reads as a horizontal, layered armature mediating between street and water.

category_critiques.concept_originality: The horizontal, layered parti is competent and legible, but at 49 dominant lines and modest visual complexity the scheme reads as a familiar river-edge typology rather than a fresh proposition; the idea is sound but not yet singular.
category_critiques.spatial_hierarchy: A strong horizontal datum (41 horizontal vs 8 vertical lines) suggests a clear circulation spine paralleling the river, though the near-total open-space ratio (0.94) leaves the sequence of public-to-quiet thresholds under-articulated, as circulation_and_spatial_order.md warns against path as leftover space.
category_critiques.transparency_light: High brightness (0.81) and white ratio (0.58) register the intended glazing and daylight, but transparency_light_and_daylight.md cautions that openness asserted as undifferentiated glass without graded modulation or shading logic is daylight unresolved rather than designed.
category_critiques.materiality_detailing: The promised timber tectonic is not legible in the image — colour variety 0.134 and saturation 0.12 read as a flat, near-monochrome palette (#bed2dd), and materiality_and_tectonics.md flags exactly this gap between named material and shown surface richness.
category_critiques.alignment_keywords: Keyword expression of 0.35 (RAG similarity 0.47) confirms the permeable ground floor and river view are gestured at but weakly substantiated; the timber structure in particular is asserted in language, not demonstrated in the representation.

recommendations: Render the timber structure explicitly — expressed columns, beams, and joinery — so materiality reads as tectonic, not finish.
Grade the glazing with shading, depth, and poche to resolve glare and privacy along the river facade.
Articulate the permeable ground floor with a hierarchy of thresholds rather than one undifferentiated open field.
Introduce vertical accents or a sectional move to relieve the dominant horizontal datum and sharpen circulation.
narrative_critique.justification: An overall 5.6/10 reflects a clear, well-composed parti with credible daylight and a legible public threshold, undercut by weak materiality and only partial keyword substantiation. Per materiality_and_tectonics.md, the named timber structure fails to register as tectonic surface richness (score 4), and per transparency_light_and_daylight.md the glazing is asserted rather than modulated, capping the transparency reading. The horizontal armature aligns with circulation_and_spatial_order.md but needs a more deliberate threshold sequence to lift the spatial and conceptual scores.
